reviewScope: Only three established chapter-five exercises: insertion, conversion and pairwise swapping. Fifteen independently authored implementations and their independent per-position oracles were reviewed and executed. This is not a claim that the chapter is complete.

questions.algorithm: Clear an inclusive interval with a width mask, then OR the fitting replacement shifted to low.
questions.review: Signed 32-bit words are treated as fixed patterns in every language. The fitting-insertion precondition is explicit. The full-width interval and bit 31 are valid and do not perform a 32-bit shift by 32. Every inclusive interval is exercised with zero, full and random fitting replacements. Negative insertion is permitted only for width 32.

questions.algorithm: XOR the two 32-bit patterns, then clear the lowest set bit once per counted difference.
questions.review: Every actual implementation clears bits rather than scanning all positions, matching its O(k), k<=32 explanation. Negative values have exactly 32 bits. The independent reference compares individual positions, including the sign bit. Zero versus minus one yields 32.

questions.algorithm: Mask even and odd positions separately, move each group into its paired positions, and OR.
questions.review: All sixteen adjacent pairs are swapped simultaneously. Each one-bit input, sign-bit movement, alternating masks and random signed words are covered. The independent reference gathers each output bit from position i XOR 1. Involution and population-preservation properties are checked separately.

languageBindingReview.csharp: uint masks give logical shifts; explicit unchecked conversions preserve signed patterns. The insertion width-32 branch avoids C# shift-count wrapping. CountBitChanges subtracts only from a nonzero uint, so its decrement cannot underflow.
languageBindingReview.javascript: Bitwise operations operate on signed 32-bit values; >>> supplies logical shifts and unsigned normalization where needed. The insertion mask uses exact powers of two up to 2^32 before coercion, avoiding shift-count wrapping. Results are checked as signed 32-bit integers.
languageBindingReview.python: Inputs are masked to 32 bits before XOR counting and mask movement, and high-bit results are converted back by subtracting 2^32. Thus unbounded sign extension cannot create an infinite bit-clearing loop or an unsigned result alias.
languageBindingReview.cpp: Unsigned uint32_t patterns avoid signed-shift overflow. Insertion uses uint64_t so a shift by width 32 is defined. Conversion to a negative signed result first subtracts 2^32 in signed long long, then narrows only a value already in int range. This avoids relying on implementation-defined unsigned-to-signed narrowing.
languageBindingReview.java: Insertion uses a 64-bit mask for width 32 and explicitly masks signed inputs into their 32-bit patterns. Pairwise swapping uses >>> rather than >>. Java's defined two's-complement int arithmetic makes lowest-bit clearing correct even when the sign bit is set.
